rounds.response: Heartburn is the sensation of burning behind the breastbone caused when stomach contents (including acid) reflux into and irritate the esophagus—this is commonly called gastroesophageal reflux (GER/GERD). Triggers can include late or large meals, lying down soon after eating, spicy or fatty foods, alcohol/caffeine, certain medications, obesity, and anatomical issues, so avoiding late spicy meals and not lying down often helps but isn’t a guaranteed 100% cure. Many people with mild, occasional heartburn manage symptoms with lifestyle changes and occasional over‑the‑counter antacids, but ongoing or worsening symptoms may need evaluation and prescription treatment or testing. If you have alarm signs (difficulty swallowing, vomiting, unexplained weight loss, black stools, or chest pain), seek prompt medical attention. A useful next step people use is to keep a brief log of what you eat, when symptoms occur, and your position (standing/lying) to share with a clinician if you decide to discuss it.
